summary: Sprawling across nearly 20 square miles of the narrow corridor between the Santa Ana Mountains and the Temescal Mountains in western Riverside County, Temescal Valley packs fewer than 1,500 people per square mile into a landscape shaped by the ancient wash that gives it its name — a geography that means many homes sit against dramatic hillside backdrops while daily errands require a car and Interstate 15. That freeway is the defining feature: it funnels tens of thousands of commuters toward job centers in Irvine, Corona, and beyond, making this firmly a bedroom community where switching employers almost certainly means switching commute directions. The affordability math looks manageable on paper — a median home value around $648,000 against a median household income near $120,000 puts the price-to-income ratio at roughly 5.4, tight but not crushing by Southern California standards — yet median rent above $2,790 signals that even non-buyers feel the squeeze. With nearly 10 hours of daily sunshine and an average high of 77°F, the climate is relentlessly pleasant, ideal for the surrounding open-space trails threading through sage-scrub hills. Temescal Valley is essentially a sun-drenched commuter corridor that traded urban convenience for elbow room and ridgeline sunsets.
